
# Implementation Plan: MetaCTF Bot Solver

**Branch**: `001-metactf-bot-solver` | **Date**: 2025-12-13 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/001-metactf-bot-solver/spec.md`

**Note**: This plan is generated by `/speckit.plan` and follows the project constitution.

## Summary

Build a Python 3.14 bot that uses Playwright to automate login, scraping, and solving of MetaCTF.com problems. Credentials and target environment are loaded from `.env`. The bot logs in, selects the correct CTF environment, scrapes all active problems (with links and files) to `data/metactf/<date>/`, analyzes them for MetaCTF{flag} patterns, and submits found flags. All code is simple, well-logged, and never runs headless unless directed.

**Language/Version**: Python 3.14 (venv required)
**Primary Dependencies**: Playwright (browser automation), requirements.txt or pyproject.toml for all Python deps
**Storage**: Local filesystem (data/metactf/<date>/)
**Testing**: pytest (recommended), Playwright for browser tests
**Target Platform**: Windows (PowerShell 5.1 compatibility required)
**Project Type**: Single project (CLI + services + models)
**Performance Goals**: MVP: Complete scrape and solve cycle for all problems in <10 minutes (adjust as needed)
**Constraints**: No direct work on main branch; frequent, descriptive commits; no headless chromedriver unless directed
**Scale/Scope**: MVP: Single user, single environment, all active problems

### Source Code (repository root)

```text
src/
  models/         # Data classes: Credentials, Problem, Flag
  services/       # Scraping, solving, submission logic
  cli/            # CLI entrypoint for the bot
  lib/            # Utilities (file ops, regex, logging)
tests/
  contract/       # Contract tests for scraping/solving
  integration/    # End-to-end tests
  unit/           # Unit tests for helpers
data/
  metactf/<date>/ # Scraped problems and files
```

**Structure Decision**: Single-project layout with clear separation of CLI, services, models, and utilities. All scraped data is stored under `data/metactf/<date>/` for traceability and debugging.
